## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to detect fixed bit patterns with pure bitwise ops, no loops or conditionals, reinforcing shifts, masking, and truthiness evaluation.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts align neighboring bits
- Combining with AND tests multiple bit conditions simultaneously
- Pure bitwise approach scales to fixed-width inputs without branching

## Code Example
```c
bool hasPattern101(uint32_t n) {
  return (n & (n >> 2) & ~(n >> 1)) != 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit inputs?
- What edge cases exist near the topmost bits (i=29) and how does masking affect them?

Tests constant-time bit manipulation skills, branchless thinking, and understanding of 64-bit mask patterns.

- **Pairwise masks**: `0x5...` (alternating `0101`) isolates even bits; `0xA...` (alternating `1010`) isolates odd bits

- **Performance verification**: benchmark against naive loop-based implementations to confirm O(1) constant-time behavior

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to apply fixed-width bit twiddling to real data without loops, a common pattern in systems programming.

uint32_t swapAdjacentBytes32(uint32_t x) {
